fact: The World Bank approved on 15 June 2026 a US$120 million project (US$100m IDA credit, US$20m grant) that will promote integration of the social registry with other databases, including those for internally displaced persons and health insurance.

The World Bank page states work has been initiated to support interoperability between the databases of the Social Registry, internally displaced persons and the Unique Identifier System being developed under the WURI project; no event date given, published date used.
The World Bank Board approved US$120 million on 15 June 2026 for a project that finances integration of the Registre Social Unique with the IDP, health-insurance and other key beneficiary databases.

The World Bank appraisal document says Component 2 of the proposed Economic Opportunities for Resilience Project supports development of interoperable systems, including social registries and Government payment platforms, and sets an outcome indicator on databases or systems connected to the social registry.

The document says the RSU and the internally displaced persons data are managed separately, while coordination efforts are under way; date is the document's published date, as it gives none for the statement.

The document says the social registry is a gateway for various social programs to select their beneficiaries, and that PAMPV economic inclusion beneficiaries will be selected from the RSU database; it states the RSU covers about one-quarter of poor and vulnerable households and is rolled out in 10 regions.
